```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

The mosaics of one Time-SIFT chunk are consistent with each other, but two chunks, or two drones, can be shifted by
some decimetres to metres (the GPS of the drones is not more accurate). Following a tree crown over time needs
mosaics that overlay to a few centimetres: `align_mosaics()` co-registers all the mosaics of a series with
[AROSICS](https://github.com/GFZ/arosics) (Scheffler et al. 2017).

## How it works

For each mosaic (the *target*):

1. a **reference** is chosen (see the three modes below), aggregated to 0.5 m and converted to grey (mean of the RGB
   bands; the white background is ignored). At 5 cm the result is practically the same, many times slower;
2. AROSICS measures the shift between the target and the reference on a **grid of tie points** (one every 200
   pixels of the target, i.e. 10 m at 5 cm), by correlation of 200 x 200 pixel windows, and removes the unreliable
   points;
3. the shifts, interpolated between the points, are **applied to the whole target**, at its own resolution: the
   aligned mosaic is written in `out_dir`, with the same file name.

## One transformation per chunk

The mosaics of one Time-SIFT chunk of `generate_mosaics()` have the same geometry: the same shifts align them all
on a given reference. When the mosaics come from `generate_mosaics()` (its `plan.csv` is found next to the
`orthomosaics` folder), `align_mosaics()` therefore measures the shifts **once per chunk and per reference**, on the
mosaic of the chunk that covers the largest area (if it fails, on the next one, up to 3), and applies them to the
other mosaics of the chunk. Measuring the shifts is the longest step: a series of 100 dates in 11 chunks needs 11
measures instead of 100.

This is only valid for mosaics of the **same chunk** aligned on the **same reference**: in mode `"nearest"`, the
mosaics of a chunk with different nearest references get one measure per reference; mosaics not in the plan are
measured one by one. The column `transform_from` of the journal gives, for each mosaic, the mosaic on which its
shifts were measured. `share_by_chunk = FALSE` measures every mosaic (for example to check that a chunk is
consistent); `plan = "..."` gives the plan when it is elsewhere.

## Mode `"previous"`: each date on the one before (default)

```{r}
library(canobsR)
align_mosaics("D:/bouamir/2_mosaics/orthomosaics", "D:/bouamir/3_aligned")
```

The mosaics are taken in chronological order (date in the file name; with one transformation per chunk, the chunks
in the order of their measured mosaics). The first one is the **anchor** of the series: it is copied as it is (with
the mosaics of its chunk). Each next mosaic is aligned on the **last mosaic already aligned** that covers at least
90 % of the site (of the largest mosaic): a partial flight is aligned, but is not used as a reference. The whole series is
thus brought onto the geometry of the first date, step by step, each date being compared with a recent one (similar
vegetation, similar light).

To bring the series onto an external reference (for example an orthophoto with ground control points), give it:
the first mosaic is then aligned on it, and the others follow.

```{r}
align_mosaics("D:/bouamir/2_mosaics/orthomosaics", "D:/bouamir/3_aligned",
              reference = "D:/bouamir/reference/ortho_gcp_2022.tif")
```

## Mode `"fixed"`: all the dates on one reference

```{r}
align_mosaics("D:/bouamir/2_mosaics/orthomosaics", "D:/bouamir/3_aligned_lidar",
              mode = "fixed", reference = "D:/bouamir/lidar/canopy_model_2022.tif")
```

Each mosaic is aligned directly on the same reference, so errors cannot accumulate along the series. The reference
can be an RGB mosaic or a single-band raster, such as a lidar canopy height model: AROSICS then matches the grey
level of the mosaic with the shapes of the crowns of the model. Works best when the reference and the mosaics are
not too different (season, resolution).

## Mode `"nearest"`: a set of dated references

```{r}
align_mosaics("D:/bouamir/2_mosaics/orthomosaics", "D:/bouamir/3_aligned_refs",
              mode = "nearest", reference = "D:/bouamir/references")
```

`reference` is a folder of rasters with a date in their file name (`ref_20220115.tif`, `ref_20230120.tif`, ...).
Each mosaic is aligned on the closest one in time, before or after (the one before if two are as close): useful for
long series with one reference per year or per season.

## Results, interruptions, failures

In `out_dir`: the aligned mosaics, `align_journal.csv`, `tie_points/` (the tie points of each measure: position,
shift, reliability), `transforms/` (the shifts measured, applied to the other mosaics of the chunk) and `_references/` (the grey 0.5 m references, kept to save time when running again).

```{r}
j <- read.csv("D:/bouamir/3_aligned/align_journal.csv")
j[, c("epoch", "reference", "status", "n_points", "shift_x_m", "shift_y_m")]
plot(as.Date(as.character(j$date), "%Y%m%d"), sqrt(j$shift_x_m^2 + j$shift_y_m^2),
     xlab = "date", ylab = "median shift corrected (m)")
```

`status` is `anchor`, `done` or `failed` (with the error in `message`): a mosaic fails when fewer than 10 tie points
are reliable (clouds, haze, flight over another area, very different season): it is then not used as a reference.
Like `generate_mosaics()`, **running the same command again resumes** after an interruption and retries the failed
mosaics only.

## Options

Advanced options of `align_mosaics()` (see `?align_mosaics`), with the values used on the canobs sites:

| Option | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `ref_resolution` | 0.5 | resolution of the grey reference (m) |
| `min_ref_coverage` | 0.9 | `"previous"`: minimum coverage of a reference, relative to the largest mosaic |
| `grid_res` | 200 | distance between tie points, pixels of the mosaic |
| `window_size` | 200 | size of the matching windows, pixels |
| `max_shift` | 60 | largest shift searched, pixels |
| `max_iter` | 100 | iterations of the matching |
| `n_cores` | `"auto"` | parallel processes: processors minus a few, limited by the memory (each process holds a copy of the mosaic band used for matching, ~2.5 GB for 300 ha at 5 cm); an argument of the function |
| `max_memory_gb` | 75 % of the RAM | memory that AROSICS may use, for `n_cores = "auto"` |
| `min_points` | 10 | fewer reliable tie points: failure |
| `epochs` | all | names of the mosaics to align, e.g. `c("20220427", "20220511")` |
| `share_by_chunk` | TRUE | one measure per chunk and reference (needs `plan.csv`) |
| `plan` | found | `plan.csv` of `generate_mosaics()` |
| `max_candidates` | 3 | mosaics of a chunk tried in turn if the measure fails |
